name: diagram-chat
description: Interactive Mermaid diagrams and Apache ECharts charts beside VS Code chat: ask @diagram to draw, chart CSV, JSON or command output, and edit diagrams in Markdown.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Charts of a shell command's output and chart options with JavaScript code need a trusted workspace. Reading workspace and data files, and opening a diagram's file links, ask for confirmation first.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Charts of a shell command's output are not available in virtual workspaces.

chatParticipants.name: diagram
chatParticipants.description: Draw, change and explain diagrams and charts

commands.name: new
commands.description: Start a new diagram or chart instead of changing the current one

commands.name: explain
commands.description: Explain the current diagram or chart, or the selected parts

disambiguation.description: The user wants to draw, visualize, update or explain a diagram, such as a flowchart, sequence diagram, class diagram, state machine, entity relationship diagram, architecture overview, mind map, timeline or Gantt chart.
examples: Draw a sequence diagram of the login flow
Visualize the class hierarchy in this file
Make a flowchart of this algorithm
Add error handling to the diagram

disambiguation.description: The user wants to visualize data as a chart, such as a pie chart, bar chart, line chart, scatter plot, treemap, sankey, heatmap, radar chart, box plot, gauge or funnel, with the data given inline, in a file or as the output of a shell command.
examples: Render this data as a pie chart
Bar chart of the lines of code per folder
Plot the CSV file as a line chart
Show the disk usage of these directories as a pie chart
Treemap of the file sizes under src

languageModelTools.name: diagram_render
languageModelTools.userDescription: Show a Mermaid diagram or an ECharts chart in an interactive panel
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Show a Mermaid 12 diagram (flowchart, sequence, class, state, ER, Gantt, mind map, architecture-beta, etc.) or an Apache ECharts 6 option (no maps) in the panel beside chat, replacing the current one, where the user can select items and send follow-ups. Returns the diagram type or the render error to fix. To change the current diagram, use diagram_edit; to chart a file, command output or table, use diagram_chart.

source.description: Complete Mermaid source, or an ECharts option as JSON or a JavaScript object literal with callbacks (formatter, renderItem, symbolSize, etc.); prefer templates such as "{b}: {c}" for plain formatters. Omit click directives and HTML, and colors and fonts unless the user asks for them: the panel applies the theme and sizing, and its background follows the VS Code theme. To color items of the current Mermaid diagram, use diagram_style. For a diagram type or chart kind you are unsure of, read its diagram_guide topic first.

language.description: Defaults to "echarts" for a source starting with "{", else "mermaid".

title.description: Short title shown in the panel.

clickPrompt.description: Chat request sent for the user when they click an item, with {label} replaced by its label, e.g. "Explain {label} in more detail". For explorable overviews.

links.description: Mermaid node ids mapped to code locations that clicking them opens, absolute or relative to the first workspace folder, with optional lines: {"parse": "src/parser.ts#L42", "check": "src/checker.ts#L10-L30"}. Link only code you have read.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_edit
languageModelTools.userDescription: Change the current diagram or chart with exact replacements in its source
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Change the current Mermaid diagram or ECharts chart with exact text replacements in its source, keeping the rest, node ids, the user's edits, the title, code links and click prompt, rather than sending it all again with diagram_render. Copy each oldText exactly from the source that diagram_getState gives; if any edit does not apply, nothing changes and the result quotes the closest lines. Returns what changed, or the render error with the lines around it. On a chart made by diagram_chart, edit only its styling: change its type, columns or data with diagram_updateChart or diagram_chart.

oldText.description: Exact text of the source, with its indentation and line breaks, that occurs once unless replaceAll is set.

edits.description: Replacements made in order, each in the source that those before it left; all or none are made. Keep each oldText short but unique, e.g. [{"oldText": "A --> B", "newText": "A --> C[Cache] --> B"}].

revision.description: Revision from diagram_getState or the result of the tool call that drew the diagram; the edits are refused if it has changed since.

title.description: New title shown in the panel; omit to keep it.

links.description: Code links to add or change, by Mermaid node id, as in diagram_render, e.g. {"cache": "src/cache.ts#L12"}; null removes one. The others are kept.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_chart
languageModelTools.userDescription: Chart data given inline, in a file or as a command's output
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Chart tabular data with Apache ECharts in the panel beside chat, replacing the current diagram. Give exactly one of data, file or command, e.g. a treemap of `du -ah src`. Reports how it read the columns. Sizes and durations are read as bytes and seconds, the units of max and filter values. For callbacks such as renderItem or full control of the option, use diagram_render.

type.description: horizontalBar suits long labels; treemap/sunburst sum children; sankey links source and target labels, or labels to a node per value column; heatmap pivots two label columns or uses value columns as columns; radar has an axis per value column; boxplot shows each group's spread; gauge shows one value; funnel orders stages by value; histogram bins the raw numbers of one value column, without labelColumn, aggregate, sort or limit.

title.description: Short title shown in the panel.

data.description: Inline data: CSV, TSV, JSON (an array of objects or arrays, an object mapping names to numbers, or JSON Lines), a Markdown table or whitespace-separated columns.

file.description: Path, absolute or relative to the first workspace folder.

command.description: Shell command whose standard output is the data, run by /bin/sh (cmd.exe on Windows) in the first workspace folder, or else the home folder, once the user confirms.

format.description: "auto" (default) detects the format, including Markdown tables; "json" includes JSON Lines.

labelColumn.description: Label column by header or generated name, e.g. "Column 2"; defaults to the first text column naming each row, or for a boxplot grouping rows. Several, outermost first, give treemap/sunburst levels, sankey stages (source, target), heatmap rows/columns, or a bar, line or area chart's categories and a series per label of the second, for rows such as month,region,sales. Treemap, sunburst and sankey also split paths such as "src/a/b.ts" into levels. Dates such as 2026-01-02, 2026-01, 2026/01/02 and ISO times give bar, line, area and scatter charts a time axis; other dates and plain years stay labels.

valueColumns.description: One series each, or the first alone with a series per label. Defaults to numeric columns except identifiers (id, rank, pid, etc.) and units differing from the first. Pie, doughnut, treemap, sunburst, gauge and funnel use the first, scatter the first two (x, y), boxplot its raw numbers.

max.description: Top of a gauge's scale or of every radar axis; inferred by default.

aggregate.description: Combine rows with the same labels, before sort and limit. "count" counts rows and needs no value column, e.g. one row per commit. Omit for boxplot, which summarizes raw groups.

sort.description: After grouping, by the first value column, or by the total in stacked charts or with a series per label of a second label column.

limit.description: Keep the first rows after sorting; pie/doughnut combine the other positive rows as "Other".

options.description: ECharts option to merge: objects merge, null removes a setting, other values replace it. A "series" object applies to every series, and an array merges by index, e.g. {"series": [{"label": {"show": false}}]}. Omit colors, backgrounds and fonts unless the user asks for them. JSON only; for callbacks use diagram_render.

clickPrompt.description: Chat request sent for the user when they click an item, with {label} replaced by its name, e.g. "Which files make {label} so large?".

bins.description: Number of equal-width bins; by default about √n of a round width.

facetColumn.description: Split a bar, line, area, scatter or histogram chart into a panel per value of this column (at most 12), after filtering; aggregate, sort and limit apply per panel. It is not inferred as a label or value column.

facetColumns.description: Facet panels per row; automatic by default, and raised so that the panels take at most 4 rows; the view also shows more per row when rows would be too short to read at its height.

facetScales.description: Facet panels share axis ranges by default.

filters.description: Keep rows matching all filters, before anything else. Compares parsed cells: eq/neq need the exact value and type (null matches missing cells); lt/lte/gt/gte need numeric cells and a number; contains matches text case-sensitively.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_getState
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read the diagram shown in the diagram panel, with your edits and selection
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Read the panel's current diagram or chart: source, revision, chart parameters, code links, render error, user edits, marks, selected items, and the ids of same-named chart items and of edges or sequence messages between the same nodes. Use before changing a diagram you have not seen, or when the user refers to "this", "these" or the selection.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_getImage
languageModelTools.userDescription: Show the model an image of the diagram or chart in the diagram panel
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Return a PNG of the current diagram or chart as the panel draws it, in the user's theme but without selection or marks, to check its layout, such as overlapping, cut-off or unreadable labels, and fix it. The result says what the image shows at what scale, and when its text is too small to read: then give "ids" to see the part around those items larger. Call only if you can view images.

ids.description: Show only the part around these items: Mermaid node ids, edges or sequence messages by their ends' node ids as "A --> B" (all between those nodes) or "A --> B: label", or chart item names. Omit for the whole drawing.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_guide
languageModelTools.userDescription: Look up how to draw a kind of Mermaid diagram or ECharts chart well
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Return a guide to a Mermaid 12 diagram type or ECharts 6 chart kind: an example that renders in the panel, the syntax rules models get wrong, layout tips and what the panel does already. Without a topic, lists the topics. Use before drawing a type you are unsure of, or after a render error you can't fix.

topic.description: A diagram type such as "flowchart", "sequence", "architecture" or "gantt", or an ECharts topic such as "echarts", "echarts-bar" or "echarts-time"; omit for the list.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_pickNodes
languageModelTools.userDescription: Ask you to select nodes, relationships or chart items in the diagram panel
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Ask the user a question and wait until they click their answer in the current diagram or chart, e.g. "Which step is failing?". Returns the picked labels and ids, with endpoints for edges and sequence messages, or why nothing was picked.

prompt.description: One short question shown above the diagram.

multiple.description: Let the user pick several items and confirm with Done. Defaults to false: the first click answers.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_annotate
languageModelTools.userDescription: Mark nodes, edges, sequence messages or chart items without drawing again
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Mark items of the current diagram or chart for a walkthrough, a problem or a path, without redrawing it; say in your answer what the marks show. Each call replaces the previous marks and fading; omit marks to clear them. Marks are not part of the source and clear when a new diagram is drawn. Returns which ids were marked and which are unknown.

id.description: Exact Mermaid node id; an edge or sequence message by its ends' node ids as "A --> B", one of several between the same nodes with its label as "A --> B: Yes", or by its edge:/message: id from diagram_getState; or chart item name. Chart items that share a name need the ids diagram_getState lists for them.

mark.description: "current" (default) for the step being explained, "problem" for a failure, "good" for something working or a recommended path, "info" for a pointer.

marks.description: Omit or pass [] to clear the marks.

dim.description: Fade unmarked items. Defaults to false.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_findFiles
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Find files in all workspace folders by glob. Returns one path per line, usable as diagram_readFile's file and in code links. Skips .git, node_modules and what files.exclude, search.exclude and .gitignore files exclude.

glob.description: Glob relative to each workspace folder, e.g. "**/*.ts" or "src/**", or starting with the absolute path of one folder to match only in it, as files outside the first folder are listed. Defaults to "**/*".

languageModelTools.name: diagram_searchText
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Search workspace text files, including unsaved editor changes, for a literal string, in the files that diagram_findFiles lists. Returns matching lines with their numbers, grouped by file path. Scans at most 1000 files and 16 MiB per call; narrow the glob when it reports incomplete results.

query.description: Literal text on one line, not a regular expression.

glob.description: Glob relative to each workspace folder, e.g. "**/*.ts" or "src/**", or starting with the absolute path of one folder to match only in it, as files outside the first folder are listed. Defaults to "**/*".

languageModelTools.name: diagram_readFile
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read lines from a workspace file
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Read numbered lines from a text file in an open workspace folder, including unsaved editor changes. Use the line numbers in code links.

file.description: Path as diagram_findFiles and diagram_searchText return it: relative to the first workspace folder, or absolute.

endLine.description: Inclusive; defaults to startLine + 199. Reads at most 500 lines.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_inspectData
languageModelTools.userDescription: Inspect columns and sample rows from the current chart or another data source
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Report a data source's columns, inferred types, row count and sample rows without drawing. Omit the source to inspect the current chart's loaded data, or give exactly one of data, file or command as for diagram_chart, which reads it again to chart it.

data.description: Inline data, e.g. CSV or JSON.

file.description: Path, absolute or relative to the first workspace folder.

command.description: Shell command whose standard output is the data, run once the user confirms.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_updateChart
languageModelTools.userDescription: Change the current chart's settings without reloading its data
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Change the current chart made by diagram_chart, reusing its loaded data without rereading files or rerunning commands. Settings mean the same as in diagram_chart; omitted ones are kept, except those a new type cannot use, and null clears one. Keeps supported manual styling, and refuses changes that would lose unsupported manual source edits. To change the data source, use diagram_chart.

revision.description: Revision from diagram_getState or the result of the tool call that drew the chart; the update is refused if the chart has changed since.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_style
languageModelTools.userDescription: Set the fill, border and text colors of nodes, subgraphs, edges, classes, states or ER entities in the Mermaid diagram
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Color items of the current Mermaid diagram, only when the user asks for colors: flowchart nodes, subgraphs and edges, classes, states and ER entities, by their style and linkStyle lines, keeping the rest of the source. Sets fill, stroke (a border, or an edge's line) and text, which defaults to black or white, whichever reads on the fill. Take the ids from the source or the selection that diagram_getState gives. The panel background follows the VS Code theme and cannot be changed.

id.description: Exact Mermaid id of a node, subgraph, class, state or entity, as in the source, or a flowchart edge by its ends' ids as "A --> B", with its label as "A --> B: Yes" where several go between them.

fill.description: Background as a CSS color: a name, #rgb, #rrggbb, #rrggbbaa, rgb() or hsl(). null removes it; omit to keep it.

stroke.description: Border as a CSS color. null removes it; omit to keep it.

text.description: Label color as a CSS color, or "auto" for black or white, whichever contrasts more with the fill; a translucent fill leaves it to the panel. Defaults to "auto" with a fill. null removes it; removing the fill removes it too unless given.

clear.description: true removes the item's whole style line. Give no colors with it.

revision.description: Revision from diagram_getState or the result of the tool call that drew the diagram; the change is refused if the diagram has changed since.

diagram.codeLens.enabled.markdownDescription: Show an **Open in Diagram** action above every `mermaid` and `echarts` code block and `::: mermaid` container in a Markdown file, which opens the diagram in the panel. The **Diagram: Open Diagram at Cursor** command opens one without it.

scripts.pretest: npm run compile && npm run compile-tests
